comparison: Both evaluations address transmission intensity effects on repertoire structure (C3, C26-C29, C43). OpenEval finds these claims fully supported by model simulations in Figures 2-3. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm this finding, stating the model shows 'the degree of structuring depends on transmission intensity.' Complete agreement on this aspect.

Both address empirical analyses of var gene patterns (C35-C40, C4). OpenEval expresses uncertainty due to small sample size (n=30) and inability to definitively rule out alternative explanations. Peer reviewers explicitly support the empirical contribution, affirming that 'linkage disequilibrium among the latter cannot be attributed to demographic forces alone' without raising concerns about sample size or interpretation.

Both address predictions about malaria elimination and control implications (C46-C48, C50-C52). OpenEval considers these speculative predictions not yet validated. Peer reviewers express skepticism about elimination claims, stating 'It is not obvious' that the findings explain difficulty of malaria elimination, and request further development of clinical/control implications. Both agree these claims require additional support.

Both address model specification and parameters (C55-C63). OpenEval finds the model clearly specified with reasonable assumptions despite simplifications. Peer reviewers express concerns about clarity and potential errors, noting 'Parts of the Materials and methods are difficult to follow' and questioning the mathematical formulation of repertoire calculations. Disagreement on adequacy of model specification.

Both address age-structured immunity patterns (C31-C34). OpenEval finds these supported by model simulations in Figures 4-5, with patterns emerging logically from model assumptions. Peer reviewers do not question these findings and request extension of implications, indicating acceptance of underlying immunity patterns. Agreement on these claims.

Both address punctuated turnover dynamics (C20-C22). OpenEval finds these supported by model simulations in Figure 1, robust to different parameters. Peer reviewers acknowledge the finding but express uncertainty about mechanistic basis, questioning whether sequential expression is necessary for this phenomenon and noting it differs from deterministic model behavior. Partial disagreement on interpretation.

Both address core model findings about self-organization (C2, C23-C24). OpenEval finds these consistently supported by simulations and robust to alternative formulations. Peer reviewers acknowledge the theoretical contribution but raise critical questions about whether sequential expression is necessary for key dynamics, indicating uncertainty about mechanistic basis despite accepting the phenomenon itself.

Both address diversity constraints and strain structure (C25, C41-C42). OpenEval finds these supported by model simulations. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm this finding, stating the model demonstrates 'immune selection can cause the parasite population to self-organise into a finite number of strains with non-overlapping var repertoires.' Complete agreement.

Minimal overlap on C45 (age-structured immunity). OpenEval supports age-immunity patterns. Peer R8 focuses on life-long immunity assumption (C58), requesting evaluation of model robustness given evidence that malaria affects adults. Different focus areas with peer expressing concern about a key assumption.

Both address main empirical conclusion (C4). OpenEval expresses uncertainty due to small sample size and correlational nature of evidence. Peer reviewers explicitly support the empirical analyses without raising these concerns. Clear disagreement on confidence level for empirical findings.

OpenEval R8 addresses background claims about prior work (C5-C6), finding them accurately represented with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/context claims.

OpenEval R9 addresses established background knowledge about P. falciparum biology and var genes (C7-C19), finding them well-supported by literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
OpenEval R10 addresses accurate representation of prior Chen et al. 2011 findings (C49). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this citation of prior work.

OpenEval R11 addresses speculative generalization to other pathogen systems (C54), finding it unsupported hypothesis for future work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this generalization claim.

OpenEval R12 addresses methodological specifications and molecular marker knowledge (C64-C70), finding them appropriately supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological details.
